rationale: Round 1 built, ran correctly, and hit no ICE fallback, so this candidate pushes obfuscation强度 upward while keeping the cost dimensions conservative on the hot numeric kernels (Crystal_Cholesky, Crystal_div, Crystal_pow dominate the 5.1KB text and all runtime). SUB stays near-maximal across dimensions since instruction substitution is cheap, safe, and effective on arithmetic-heavy code like Cholesky/div/pow; SPLIT and IGV keep high cost-dimension weights because they add diversity at negligible runtime/size expense. FLA and BCF get elevated SecurityGain/DiversityGain for stronger control-flow resistance but restrained RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so the selector avoids stacking them onto the tight inner loops where flattening and bogus branches would hurt most. ICALL remains a strong mid-cost option for the driver/init call sites, and IBR is kept at moderate levels since indirect branches add anti-disassembly value but with higher correctness sensitivity; CorrectnessRisk weights stay >=0.6 everywhere so the selector only applies riskier transforms to functions whose features genuinely tolerate them.
